messages.author: 4311c98ec60f6b74
messages.subject: build genetic map of biparental DH population
parts:
Dear Karl,

this is rami a student working with Bernardo Ordas Lopez. Thank you very much for developing R/QTL2. It is very useful to me.

we have a biparental population of DHs in maize. we have genotyped the
population with 6000+ SNPs and this summer we will phenotype the
population. we are starting to prepare the genotypic data to analyze.

we are going to use R/QTL2, but my main doubt is about the genetic map.
I suppose that I need a genetic map before carrying out the QTL
analysis. So, first I have to estimate the genetic map and then a will
use the genetic map and the phenotypic data for the QTL analysis, is
this correct? Does the program calculate the genetic map (cM distance
between all markers) or I have to make the map with another software?
In that case which program do you recommend? With 6000 markers
MapMaker is giving me problems (I have used this program but with only
few hundreds of markers)

A second doubt is about the number of SNPs, is 6000 too high for the
QTL analysis?

thank you very much for your attention
best wishes 
rami

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: build genetic map of biparental DH population
parts:
I would start with the physical map in Mbp, or maybe use the cM:Mbp relationship for maize to get an approximate map.

You can estimate the inter-marker genetic distances in R/qtl2 with the function est_map(). It doesn't work for all cross types, but it does work for biparental doubled haploids.

6000 markers should not be too high.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: build genetic map of biparental DH population
parts:
You need to not only install the package, but each time you use it you need to type library(qtl) to load the package, so that functions such as read.cross() are available to use.

I am trying to keep R/qtl1 and R/qtl2 discussion separate. Please use the present google group for R/qtl2 questions, and join the R/qtl discussion group (https://groups.google.com/group/Rqtl-disc) and submit questions about the original R/qtl package there.

karl
